notes.307:
(ø) Major items indicated by (ø) are stored, issued, and reviewed under “Major
Items,” S. N. L. No. G–1. The standard list price given herein is for
the Mk. VIII Tank without Equipment and Spare Parts and does not
include the cost of handling, etc.

(*) Items indicated by (*) are manufacturing components which are essential
to the completion of the original unit assembly of the major product,
but as it is not practicable nor advisable to replace such parts in the
field as individual items, they will not be issued for field maintenance
except as components of the authorized assemblies listed herein. Such
items will not be reported to Field Service but will be held subject to
disposition by the Manufacturing Service. The starred items included
under assemblies as components thereof are not shown as individual
parts in the list, but when such parts are not included as components
of any assembly they are listed in their regular alphabetical arrangement.
This method of listing starred items is for the purpose of showing all
component parts necessary to complete the unit assembly and thereby
establish a name for each and for checking purposes, etc. The total
quantity of starred items required to complete the unit assembly is
shown in parenthesis.

(R) See (X) note.

(X) Items are classified as directed in Army Regulations No. 35–6540, the
letter (X) indicating expendable items, the letter (R) indicating repair
material, and items not marked with either (X) or (R) are classified as
nonexpendable. Expendable items, nonexpendable items, and repair
material will be issued by Post, camp or station depots to organizations
in accordance with the respective instructions embodied in the afore-
said Army Regulations. Provisions of the regulations do not apply
to the issue of items required in the repair and overhaul of supplies at
Ordnance establishments, to intra-depot transfers, to shipments to
camp, post or station depots, or to transactions between other estab-
lishments within the Ordnance Department. Also, owing to the neces-
sary financial transactions between the Ordnance Department and the
Militia Bureau when issues are made to National Guard not in active
Federal Service, such issues are also exempted from provisions of the
regulations.

(%) Parts indicated by (%) are the only parts listed hereon which the using
Service is authorized to requisition for replacement purposes. This
limitation is necessary for the proper control and conservation of parts.
In designating those parts which line organizations may draw the
following factors were considered: The skill of the average man in line
organizations, tools, equipment and facilities available, and the time
element.

(&) The parts listed hereon which the using services are authorized to draw are
indicated by (%). These same parts, and in addition thereto, such as
are indicated by (&) may also be drawn by Ordnance organizations
such as Maintenance and Heavy Maintenance Companies and others
whose facilities are equal thereto which would enable them to install
the parts requisitioned. No other parts may be drawn by such organ-
izations. All parts listed hereon except starred (*) items may be
drawn by Field Service Shops such as are maintained in San Antonio,
Panama, Philippines, Raritan Arsenal, Etc.
notes.308:
(#) Components of commercial parts not detailed on Ordnance drawings but
required for field maintenance are listed in accordance with manufac-
turers’ catalogue names and part number. Symbols composed of the
first letter or letters of manufacturers’ names are shown as a prefix with
manufacturers’ part numbers for the purpose of distinguishing those
pertaining to the various commercial products used on the MK. VIII
Tank, which are listed in this manner. Items, names of manufacturers,
and symbols are as follows:

{MANUFACTURERS}

(b) Pieces which are components of subassemblies pertaining to commercial
parts, not listed in manufacturers’ catalog, are considered as starred
items and are not listed under the various assemblies of which they
are components.

(c) Items indicated by (c) are included hereon to show complete list of parts and
equipment, but will be considered as cross references only. They are
common to two or more products handled by Group G, and, as such,
are carried and reviewed under “Items common to two or more Group
G products,” S. N. L. No. G–9.

(cp) Items indicated by (cp) are included hereon to show complete list of parts
and equipment, but will be considered as cross references only. They
are of standard Ordnance design and are common to products handled
by two or more groups; and, as such, are stored and issued by Group H,
and reviewed under “Standard chains and padlocks,” S. N. L. No. H–6.

(d) The various assemblies of the Ordnance Standard Chain are no longer
authorized for issue for replacement purposes. Their use will be con-
tinued, however, for original manufacturer. For replacement purposes
the welded chain ring has been superseded by an S hook, which is
detailed on drawing A4478. The chain will be carried in bulk and cut
and issued as required. The various chain assemblies may be issued
until the present supply is exhausted.

(e) The 40″ crowbar (claw end) B465 will be issued until the supply is exhausted.

(ee) Items indicated by (ee) are listed hereon to show complete list of parts and
equipment, but will be considered as cross references only. They are
either of standard commercial design or are common to products handled
by two or more groups; and as such, are stored and issued by Group
H, and reviewed under “Standard electrical equipment,” S. N. L. No.
H–5.
notes.309:
(ga) The items indicated by (ga) are required for use in shipping only.

(gb) Items indicated by (gb) are used on the first 100 tanks only.

(gd) A definite number is designated but number required differs in assembling.

(ge) Items indicated by (ge) are required as oversize studs for service parts only.
LQ483A replaces LQ88A and LQ484A replaces stud LQ196A.

(gf) Items indicated by (gf) are required only as oversize studs when holes in
cylinder exhaust flange are worn or are tapped oversize and replace
stud LQ303A.

(gh) Thrackray washers are interchangeable with Belleville springs of the same
inside diameter, one washer taking the place of 3 springs.

(gi) Items indicated by (gi) are required as oversize studs for service only in
place of stud LQ247A.

(gj) Items indicated by (gj) are required as oversize studs for service only in place
of stud LQ197A.

(gk) In field work the roller support angles are checked by actual count which is
made from the front to rear. They are counted by numbers consecu-
tively, 1 to 8 on the outside and 1 to 9 on the inside. The one extra
number on the inside is accounted for by the two roller inner skirting
plate angles M2175 and M2176 which corresponds with roller support
angle No. 5 M2082B or A.

(gm) The outlook turret roof plate, M2361, can not be assembled with outlook
turret assembly until assembled with tank.

(go) The components of these assemblies are identical but when assembled at
61° angle form left and right assemblies which are not interchangeable.

(gp) A total of 58 track roller assemblies are required but only 28 are required
when assembled with flange.

(gq) The assemblies indicated by (gq) require a babbitt lining which is poured in
and around a mandrel after brackets and bevel gear case are bolted to
channels, mandrel to pass through bevel gear case bearings to insure
eight main bearings being in line after assembled as listed under Frame,
with brackets and caps assembly. For that reason, the brackets and
caps are issued as individual items without babbitt.

(gt) Four (4) air-pressure gages and (12) wood screws, round head, No. 6 x ½″,
are required for first 100 tanks. For future production three gages
and nine screws are required.

(gu) No definite quantity can be designated as number required varies in
assembling.

(gv) Two accessory or ration boxes as detailed on 31–37–592 will be required for
future production, but for the first 100 tanks one accessory or ration
box and one smoke grenade box as detailed on obsolete drawing
31–37–593 with tray support removed, will be used.

(gw) The first 100 tanks assembled at Rock Island Arsenal were fitted with
engines assembled at Treco Motor Co., which carried pistons LQ466A.
Therefore, the engine assembly is listed with piston LQ466A. The new
design piston SH1020A, will be used, however, for all replacements.

(gx) By action of the Ordnance Committee, Sept. 1, 1922, O. C. M. Item 2344,
the Zenith carburetor will be substituted for the Ball and Ball carburetor.
As the Ball and Ball carburetors now in service become unserviceable,
they will be turned in to the Ordnance Officer, Tank School, Camp
Meade, Md., where they will be disassembled and serviceable parts used
in the repair of unserviceable carburetors now in tanks pending the
installation of Zenith carburetor.
notes.310:
(gy) The commercial items indicated by (gy) were furnished by concerns which
have been dissolved or no longer engaged in the manufacture of these
items. Therefore, in cases where parts lists are not available the items
are listed as a unit only, pending the adoption of substitutes which are
now under study in the Manufacturing Service. Until substitutes are
adopted, the tanks in current service will be maintained from the
limited quantity of parts available or by the removal of parts from
tanks in storage.

(gaa) When the crank shaft becomes worn and has to be remachined, it then has
to be refitted with undersize bearings as detailed on 31–ODL–127, 128,
Pc. Mk. LQ127B and LQ148B.

(gac) In order to avoid confusion, for the purpose of this list, a tap-bolt is defined
as a U. S. Std. hexagon head bolt threaded either longer or shorter than
the standard. As this threading is in accordance with special require-
ments, the tap-bolts are listed as special to this unit assembly.

(gaf) A 2″ cubical wood block is required for shipping and storage to prevent
the expansion of the piston ring in the expansion chamber. Block to
be inserted in cylinder prior to the insertion of the Piston, assembly.

(gai) The camouflage net is now obsolete, but due to expense of modification,
the brackets will not be removed.

(gaj) The old standard piston detailed on LQ466A is now superseded by Piston
detailed on SH1020A. The stock of pistons LQ466A will be retained,
however, and issued when required for new work.

(gak) According to standard practice fire extinguisher brackets should not be
riveted on but in case of the Mk. VIII Tank they are riveted to armor
plate, therefore are in reality components of the tanks. They will be
reviewed as accessories.

(gal) The first one hundred gasoline tanks which are marked for center position
only will be issued until the supply is exhausted, for replacing center
gasoline tank.

(gam) The Set of Spare Parts, Accessories, Parts for Accessories, and Addendum
covering basic spare parts will be published as Changes No. 1 to this list.

(mh) Items indicated by (mh) are included hereon to show complete list of parts
and equipment, but will be considered as cross references only. They
are either of standard commercial design or are common to products
handled by two or more groups; and as such, are stored and issued by
Group H, and reviewed under “Miscellaneous hardware,” S. N. L.
No. H–2.

(n) Items indicated by (n) are common only to the Artillery Reel, M1909MI, and
the Mk. VIII Tank. They are never to be prorated between Groups, but the
entire stock is stored and reviewed by Group C. Group G will requisi-
tion on Group C for such quantities only as may be required to fill
requisitions.

(pf) Items indicated by (pf) are included hereon to show complete list of parts
and equipment, but will be considered as cross references only. They
are either of standard commercial design or are common to products
handled by two or more groups; and, as such, are stored and issued by
Group H, and reviewed under “Standard pipe and pipe fittings,”
S. N. L. No. H–7.
